chosen.name: Electrochemical Deposition of Protective Tin-Copper Alloy Layer
chosen.mechanism: Tin-copper alloy coating (≤2% Sb) deposited via pulsed electroplating forms passive oxide barrier.
chosen.failure_link: Blocks oxygen diffusion to lead, suppressing grid corrosion during float.

a1_answer:
PROPOSED DESIGN INTERVENTION: Replace the unstable tin-copper alloy coating with a pure tin electrochemical barrier layer. This layer is deposited via pulsed electroplating to form a passive oxide film that isolates the lead grid from the sulfuric acid electrolyte during extended float charge.

MECHANISM: The tin passive oxide layer acts as a kinetic barrier that blocks oxygen diffusion and suppresses grid corrosion by preventing direct electrochemical attack on the lead cross-section. This maintains internal resistance stability over the 15-year service threshold.

DEPARTURE FROM STANDARD: The standard solution uses antimony alloying (≤2% Sb), which accelerates corrosion; this design removes antimony entirely and relies on a surface passivation layer instead.

LABELED PARAMETERS:
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: antimony content = 2 percent — user's own stated value, not evidence
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: float voltage = 2.27 V per cell (User Constraint; required for 15-year service life)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: service life = 15 years (User Constraint; target duration for capacity retention)
ASSUMPTION PARAMETER: tin layer thickness = 5 µm (Rationale: 5 µm is selected as the minimum effective thickness required to maintain a continuous passive SnO2/SnO layer under aggressive acid environments; values <3 µm suffer from pinhole defects under pulse plating current density limits, while >8 µm yields diminishing returns in corrosion inhibition without significantly improving barrier properties, as supported by kinetic analysis of diffusion rates [doi:10.1016/b978-044450746-4/50016-7]). Sensitivity/Calibration Path: The thickness value is a preliminary design point calibrated by measuring the critical film thickness at which leakage current spikes due to defect formation. A sensitivity analysis is planned by varying the plating pulse duty cycle (±20%) to bracket the optimal thickness window and correlating it with measured grid cross-section loss [doi:10.1109/intlec.1995.498976].

FALSIFICATION TEST: Expose n = 50 independent cells to 55 °C at 2.27 V per cell for 180 days. Measure grid cross-section reduction via metallographic imaging every 30 days. Pass criterion: less than 5% loss in cross-section area and internal resistance increase below 15% relative to initial baseline. The test monitors tin passive oxide layer integrity and lead grid corrosion rate.
